partners.mechanism_chain: ATP8B1 (HGNC:911) —DISRUPTS→ Phospholipid transport at plasma membrane (GO:0006899); Phospholipid transport at plasma membrane (GO:0006899) —LEADS_TO→ Intrahepatic cholestasis (HP:0003134); ATP8B1 (HGNC:911) —DECREASES→ Phospholipids (CHEBI:24100); ATP2A2 (HGNC:702) —DISRUPTS→ Calcium homeostasis (GO:0005881); Calcium homeostasis (GO:0005881) —DISRUPTS→ Intracellular calcium ions (CHEBI:29108); Intracellular calcium ions (CHEBI:29108) —LEADS_TO→ Darier disease skin lesions (HP:0008072); Phospholipids (CHEBI:24100) —LEADS_TO→ Phospholipid transport at plasma membrane (GO:0006899); Intracellular calcium ions (CHEBI:29108) —INCREASES→ Calcium homeostasis (GO:0005881). Mutations in ATP8B1 (causing BRIC1) disrupt phospholipid transport at the plasma membrane, leading to cholestasis. Separately, mutations in ATP2A2 (causing Darier disease) disrupt calcium homeostasis, leading to altered calcium levels and subsequent keratinocyte differentiation defects manifesting as skin lesions. Both genes are critical for maintaining cellular membrane integrity and ion gradients, suggesting an overlap in cellular processes that, when disrupted, lead to distinct but mechanistically related pathologies.

**Proposed mechanism:** ATP8B1 (HGNC:911) —DISRUPTS→ Phospholipid transport at plasma membrane (GO:0006899); Phospholipid transport at plasma membrane (GO:0006899) —LEADS_TO→ Intrahepatic cholestasis (HP:0003134); ATP8B1 (HGNC:911) —DECREASES→ Phospholipids (CHEBI:24100); ATP2A2 (HGNC:702) —DISRUPTS→ Calcium homeostasis (GO:0005881); Calcium homeostasis (GO:0005881) —DISRUPTS→ Intracellular calcium ions (CHEBI:29108); Intracellular calcium ions (CHEBI:29108) —LEADS_TO→ Darier disease skin lesions (HP:0008072); Phospholipids (CHEBI:24100) —LEADS_TO→ Phospholipid transport at plasma membrane (GO:0006899); Intracellular calcium ions (CHEBI:29108) —INCREASES→ Calcium homeostasis (GO:0005881). Mutations in ATP8B1 (causing BRIC1) disrupt phospholipid transport at the plasma membrane, leading to cholestasis. Separately, mutations in ATP2A2 (causing Darier disease) disrupt calcium homeostasis, leading to altered calcium levels and subsequent keratinocyte differentiation defects manifesting as skin lesions. For instance, interventions aimed at restoring normal phospholipid asymmetry or modulating intracellular calcium levels might offer benefit for both cholestatic liver diseases and Darier disease, despite their distinct primary presentations.
